notes.heading: About these points
notes.best-car-only: Only each team's best-placed car scores
notes.half-points: A race cut short paid half points, so some totals end in .5.
notes.double-points: The 2014 finale in Abu Dhabi paid double points.
notes.shared-points: Drivers who shared a car, or tied for fastest lap, split the points as they did at the time, so some totals have long decimals.
notes.shared-points-constructors: When a car or fastest lap was shared, the points were split as they were at the time, so some team totals have long decimals.
notes.sprint-assumed: This system had no sprint races; AlterF1 scores them 3-2-1 (F1's first sprint rule, 2021).
notes.best-scaled: This system counted only a driver's best results; the count is scaled to this season's length.
notes.best-scaled-constructors: This system counted only each team's best results; the count is scaled to this season's length.
notes.ineligible: Some finishers could not score (F2 cars, unregistered entries or penalties), exactly as in the real season.
notes.ineligible-constructors: Some teams or entries could not score (championship exclusions, F2 cars, unregistered entries or penalties); their points do not count.

about.title: How AlterF1 works
about.intro: AlterF1 takes the real results of every Formula 1 season and scores them again under five historical points systems. The races stay the same; only the rules that turn results into points change.
about.systemsIntro: Each system is modelled with its full rules, not just its points table.
about.system1950: Fastest lap +1. Only the best 4 results count. Shared drives split the points.
about.system1961: A best-results rule that changed from season to season (split into two halves in 1967–80).
about.system2010: Fastest lap +1 for a top-10 finisher in 2019–24. Sprint points as used in each season.
about.eraBody: In its own era each system applies that season's exact historical rules. Outside it, AlterF1 keeps the system's share of counted results: the 1961 system counts the best 11 of 16, so in 2021's 22 races it counts the best 15.
about.constructorsBody: Constructors follow the rules of the selected points system: in its own era each system applies that season's historical constructors' rules — including the 1958–78 rule where only each team's best-placed car scored — and outside it its canonical rules. Teams are grouped by chassis and engine (for example Cooper-Climax and Cooper-Maserati are scored separately), just as in the official championship. Because the constructors' championship began in 1958, earlier seasons are shown as an alternative calculation.
about.halfPointsBody: Races cut short (Belgium 2021, Spain 1975, Australia 1991) paid half points. The default "Historical" package applies them under every system, so under 1991 rules fourth place is worth 1.5 and sixth 0.5. Choose "Pure" in the scenario panel to turn them off.
about.doublePointsBody: Abu Dhabi 2014 paid double points. By default this applies only under the 2010 system.
about.fiftiesBody: Shared cars and shared fastest laps split their points exactly as they did at the time. In Britain 1954 seven drivers shared the fastest lap, 1/7 point each, so values like 0.14 can appear.
about.sprintBody: Systems without a sprint table (1950, 1961, 1991, 2003) score sprints 3-2-1, F1's first sprint rule from 2021. This is an AlterF1 assumption.
about.ineligibleBody: F2 cars (1958, 1967, 1969), unregistered second cars (1984, 1987) and post-race penalties are read from the real results and applied the same way under every system.
about.dataBody: Results come from F1DB, used under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. AlterF1 is an independent project and is not associated with Formula 1.
